edges.description: Productive intracellular replication is the prerequisite for the cytopathic ultrastructural changes later observed in infected rat brain and LLC-MK2 cells.
Cell-scale viral replication is the conserved initiating process upstream of clinically detectable systemic AHFV infection; the exact human target cell bridge has not been resolved.

Cytopathic replication is connected to the human systemic syndrome only indirectly because the cited ultrastructural work used neonatal rat brain and LLC-MK2 cells rather than primary human target tissues.
Tick bites and livestock-associated contact expose humans to AHFV, placing the exposure upstream of viral replication in newly infected cells.
The model reproduces lethal AHFV-associated central nervous system pathology, but it bypasses peripheral exposure by inoculating neonatal rats intracranially.
